Ricette tab -> favorites-list renders favorite-{id} card ('Gnocchi con bresaola e spinaci · 650 kcal · P40 C90 G12 · 200 g gnocchi, ...'); btn-remove-fav-{id} click removes the card from the DOM. Calendario tab -> start-reminder-note present ('🔔 La sera prima alle 20:00 riceverai una notifica con il menù del primo giorno…') because marco dietStartDate=2026-10-12 (scheduled). Regressione: Riepilogo, Frigo, Peso, Acqua, Umore, Foto Pasto, Profilo tabs opened sin console error (only 401 noise before login).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py send_start_reminders / send_stock_alerts gate on local hour (==20 or ==9) and minute<15; the /api/cron/reminders endpoint calls them unconditionally in a BackgroundTask -- correct, they self-skip off-hours. Good defensive design, no action needed.

server.py add_to_shopping dedupe uses case-insensitive match on name only (ignoring qty/reparto) and inserts the Integratori category at index 0 -- fine for current UX. If supp_shop_name later returns a shorter string (e.g. without variant) duplicates would still slip past; consider normalising on (reparto, name_lower).

POST /api/favorites: fav id is uuid5(user_id + title), making the title the natural key -- consistent with upsert on {user_id,title}; however the UI shows items/calories from the first save, so saving the same title with newer macros is a no-op from the user's point of view. Minor UX, consider using $set on all meal fields.

POST /api/plan/eat-out hard-codes the meal order list and uses order.index() -- if a plan was generated with an unknown key (e.g. 'merenda') the endpoint would 400 or wipe downstream. Add a safeguard that falls back to the meals' positional index inside the day.
frontend MealPlanViewer toggleFav passes the full `shown` object (which may be the alternate 'alt' meal) to POST /api/favorites -- correct, this is what the user sees. Good.
